key_insight: A parameterized physics-informed neural network predicts embedded microchannel cooling across a continuous geometric design space, with reported computational savings exceeding four orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Fast thermohydraulic predictions could accelerate the design and optimization of embedded liquid cooling for high-performance electronic chips.
method: Inputs combine four geometric dimensions with three spatial coordinates.
Geometric ansatz embedding, SOAP optimization, and a thermal-conductivity curriculum improve training convergence.
An optimized JAX implementation trains on one consumer-grade GPU in under four hours.
evidence_signal: Compared with finite-element simulations, the abstract reports relative errors of 8.1% for velocity fields and 5.6% for temperature fields.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish experimental validation or reliability outside the modeled geometric design space.
paper_title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
